headline: Anthropic sets $70-$78 IPO price range, valuing it near $1.4 trillion
summary: Anthropic moved forward with its IPO and set a price range of $70 to $78 per share, implying a valuation of roughly $1.4 trillion at the top of the range, down from an earlier expected $2 trillion target. Each of the company's seven co-founders plans to sell shares worth about $250 million while the group keeps control.

claims.statement: Anthropic moved forward with its IPO, expected to set its valuation range.

sources.quote: Anthropic reportedly plans to move forward with IPO plans
The AI company is expected to set its valuation range this week, the Wall Street Journal reported.

claims.statement: Anthropic set an IPO price range of $70 to $78 per share.

sources.quote: The AI company behind the Claude chatbot will offer its shares at between $70 and $78.
Anthropic sets IPO price range of $70 to $78 per share to reach an implied valuation of $1.404 trillion

claims.statement: At the top of that price range, the IPO would value Anthropic at roughly $1.4 trillion, short of an earlier expected $2 trillion target.

sources.quote: The company could end up being worth a hefty $1.404 trillion if its shares list at the top of the price range, on a fully diluted basis.

Anthropic is seeking a valuation of up to $1.4tn (£1.1tn) in its imminent stock market flotation , short of the $2tn that had been expected before investors started to question the durability of the AI boom.

claims.statement: A BBC report put the listing's valuation at $1.3 trillion.

sources.quote: Anthropic heads for $1.3 trillion valuation in major stock market listing

claims.statement: Each of Anthropic's seven co-founders plans to sell the same number of shares in the IPO, netting about $250 million each while the group retains control.

sources.quote: All 7 Anthropic founders will each cash out about $250M in IPO

Each of the seven co-founders plans to sell exactly the same number of shares in the IPO, which would bring each of them about $250 million in cash at the midpoint of the price range while leaving the group in control of the company.

discrepancies.explanation: One outlet puts the IPO valuation at $1.3 trillion while others put it at roughly $1.4 trillion for the same listing.
